messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: elevated fallback events from us-west -> eu-north starting 02:14 UTC, ~11% 5xxs on /v1/generate, routing anomalies detected. auto-escalate to oncall. details: policy_id=smart-routing-v3, metric=fallback_rate
PagerDutyBot: Paging Alex (oncall) for incidents channel escalation.
Alex (oncall): Ack. I'm looking. 02:15 UTC. Seeing a spike in fallback_count and increased tail latency from affected customers.
Alex (oncall): quick question — any recent policy changes? @Pete?
Pete (runtime): I pushed a hotpatch 02:08 that allowed a temporary force-assign for model variants (force-model) to unblock a canary. It should've been scoped to canary=true but I mistakenly omitted the region constraint.
Alex (oncall): ugh. so force-model applied globally?
Pete (runtime): Yes, it set variant=redwood-7b-q4f as a forced target for policy smart-routing-v3. It bypassed normal compatibility checks for kv-cache layout.
Sara (customer-ops): We're getting a handful of customer reports: elevated latency and 502s; 3 enterprise tenants experiencing degraded throughput. CS notified customers at 02:18 UTC.
Alex (oncall): Timeline: 02:08 (hotpatch) -> 02:14 (fallback surge). Looks like mismatched model variant in region caused local failures and then automated fallback to eu regions, creating cross-region loops.
Maya (SRE): Hypothesis: forced variant in us-west has a different KV cache schema; nodes return unexpected error code that triggers smart-routing fallback, which in turn rebalances to eu nodes that prefer the same variant -> loop. Also sticky-session affinity made some requests get repeatedly retried.
Pete (runtime): Confirmed in logs. sample error from us-west runtime: ```ERROR: KV_CACHE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH: expected=V2 got=V1 model=redwood-7b-q4f shard=us-west-2 node=gw-3
trace_id=tr_3b2f...
```
Alex (oncall): First mitigation: remove the global force immediately and revert to previous policy config. Command: `redwoodctl policy update smart-routing-v3 --remove-force-variant`
Alex (oncall): Running...
PagerDutyBot: Task executed by Alex at 02:22 UTC: policy update submitted.
Pete (runtime): Policy revert submitted and propagated. We're seeing fallback_rate drop but still chatter.
Maya (SRE): Next: quarantine the problematic variant in us-west to prevent any accidental selection while we rollback. `redwoodctl variant quarantine redwood-7b-q4f --region us-west-2`
Pete (runtime): Quarantine applied. Confirmed node-level guards: no new allocations to that variant in us-west.
Alex (oncall): Also enabling temporary rate-limiter on cross-region fallback to avoid loop amplification: `redwoodctl routing set-throttle --policy smart-routing-v3 --fallback-rate 0.02`
Pete (runtime): Throttle in place. Fallback attempts down 70% in last 30s.
Sara (customer-ops): CS reports latency improved for 2/3 tenants, one still seeing intermittent 503s. Sharing customer request IDs.
Louis (product): Do we have a safety check to prevent force-model from bypassing schema compatibility? If not, that's a gap we should capture for postmortem.
Pete (runtime): No automated schema-compat guard existed for that flag. I own that gap — will make a gating check.
Maya (SRE): I'll clear KV caches on affected us-west nodes to remove stale state: `for node in $(redwoodctl nodes list --region us-west-2 --filter affected); do redwoodctl node cache-clear $node; done`
Alex (oncall): Run it and post output.
Maya (SRE): Ran cache clear at 02:28 UTC. Output: `node gw-1: cache-clear ok; gw-2: cache-clear ok; gw-3: cache-clear ok`
Pete (runtime): After cache-clear, error rate dropped further. Currently 1.2% 5xx (baseline ~0.3%). Rolling restarts scheduled on two straggler hosts to flush state.
Alex (oncall): Who is taking lead for the rest of the incident and customer comms? I need to hand off after 30m.
Maya (SRE): I'll take lead for mitigation and monitoring. @Sara continue CS updates, @Pete follow up on runtime patch (add guard), @Louis coordinate postmortem scope.
Alex (oncall): Handing off at 02:35 UTC -> Maya. Notes: root cause likely human-scoped hotpatch missing region constraint + missing compatibility gate. Customer impact: subset of enterprise tenants, approximately 2,000 requests affected, spikes in tail latency and 5xxs for ~20 min.
PagerDutyBot: Handoff recorded: previous oncall Alex -> new oncall Maya at 02:35 UTC.
Maya (SRE): I'll keep the variant quarantined until we confirm a compatibility patch. Also we'll roll back the canary progression for the redwood-7b-q4f until compatibility tests pass.
Pete (runtime): Patch in repo to add schema compatibility check to `force-model` and `policy update` flows. Will open PR and backport hotfix. Estimated ETA 2 hours for code + deploy.
Sara (customer-ops): Notified affected customers with incident summary and ETA for fix at 02:40 UTC. Customers asked for runbook steps and whether there is data loss. No data loss reported.
Louis (product): For postmortem: include why guardrails lacked region-scoped enforcement, why canary rollback wasn't automatic on schema mismatch, and why cross-region throttle default allowed amplification.
Maya (SRE): Monitoring: dashboards stable; fallback_rate trending down to baseline. Will keep incident channel open until all alerts clear and PR merges.
Alex (oncall): Thanks team. Quick reminder: avoid manual `force-*` without explicit region and schema checks.
Pete (runtime): Agreed. Also adding an alert rule to flag `KV_CACHE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` as high-sev.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation steps applied: reverted force-model, quarantined variant in us-west-2, cleared caches, applied fallback throttle, scheduled restarts. Impact window ~02:14-02:34 UTC. Postmortem owner: Louis.
Maya (SRE): Closing handoff - I'll update this thread with postmortem link once drafted.
Sara (customer-ops): Closing CS loop for reported tenants; monitoring for any fresh reports. :white_check_mark:
Pete (runtime): PR #4825 opened: add schema guard on force-model (link: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4825).
Alex (oncall): Marking resolved for initial paging. If anything flares, re-open channel. Good job. :thumbsup:
